summary: STS session tag truncation causing GCP->AWS federated agent to lose env attributes during LLM sandbox bootstrap
description:
Issue summary:
During a routine bootstrap for the LLM prod sandbox agent that federates identity from GCP (Workload Identity Federation) to AWS (STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity), the resulting STS session is missing critical session tags (env, namespace, requestor) expected by the environment-provisioner. Without these tags the provisioner falls back to the default namespace which does not have the delegated IAM role bindings, causing subsequent role assumption and k8s namespace operations to fail with AccessDenied.

Impact:
- New prod sandbox agent bootstraps failing for a subset of federated GCP service identities (approx. 12% of recent onboarding flows).
- Affected flows are time-sensitive debugging and oncall escalations that rely on ephemeral sandbox workspaces.
- Errors surface as immediate permission errors when calling AWS STS or when the provisioner attempts to map session tags to RBAC bindings.

Environment:
- Federation path: GCP WIF -> Redwood broker -> AWS STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
- Affected regions: us-east (us-east1/us-east-1 endpoints)
- Services: env-provisioner (k8s namespace bootstrap), llm-proxy (dedicated proxy that needs namespace-scoped credentials)

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use a GCP service account with the current WIF configuration and produce an id_token via gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create-cred or equivalent.
2) Exchange id_token for AWS STS credentials using AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity through our broker service (same invocation path used by onboarding scripts).
3) Inspect the STS GetCallerIdentity and the response session tags. Observe missing or truncated tag values for keys: "env", "namespace", "requestor_id" when the combined session tag payload exceeds AWS session tag size limit.
4) Trigger env-provisioner bootstrap with those credentials. It will log mapping failures and fall back to default namespace, then fail k8s rolebinding creation with AccessDenied (403) from the k8s API gateway.

Observed errors / logs (sanitized):
- broker: WARN assume_role_response: session_tags_truncated=true size=2310 max_allowed=2048
- env-provisioner: ERROR map_session_tags: missing required tag "namespace"; fallback=default-ns
- k8s-apiserver: Forbidden: User "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/redwood-sandbox/*" cannot create resource "rolebindings" in API group "rbac.authorization.k8s.io" in the namespace "default-ns"

Initial hypothesis:
- Our broker constructs session tags by serializing context attributes (project, env, namespace, requestor) and occasionally appends experimental metadata (feature_flags) for debugging. In high-tag-count flows the resulting payload exceeds AWS per-session tag size or per-tag name/value length limits, causing STS to silently drop/truncate tags. The provisioner is brittle and relies on exact tags being present.

Temporary workaround applied:
- Rolled a broker-side change (hotfix) to disable experimental feature_flags tagging in the production token path for federated WIF flows to reduce tag payload size. This change was deployed to broker-prod-canary on 2026-03-11 at 02:40 UTC. Initial replays show the immediate failure rate dropped from 12% to ~1.5%.

Next steps / proposed fix:
- Implement deterministic compacting of session tags in broker: map long attribute names to short keys (env->e, namespace->ns, requestor_id->rid) and enforce per-tag and total-tag-size validation before calling STS. (PR in progress: see related_github_prs).
- Harden env-provisioner to tolerate missing tags: add a fallback resolution path that queries the onboarding metadata store (with proper auth) rather than assume fallback to a permissive default namespace.
- Add autosynth unit tests and an integration test that simulates WIF->STS with synthetic large tag payloads to prevent regressions.

Business risk / priority justification:
- This blocks ephemeral sandbox creation used by SRE and Platform engineers for incident debugging; high priority for oncall effectiveness. No active customer production inference endpoints are affected at present, but the inability to spin sandboxes slows incident response and developer productivity.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 14:12 UTC - Triage: Observed spike in env-provisioner failures coincident with several new sandbox onboards.
2026-03-10 15:03 UTC - Collected STS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity responses and noticed broker log entry: 'session_tags_truncated=true'.
2026-03-10 16:21 UTC - Reproduced locally using a WIF token with artificially inflated feature_flags list; STS dropped tags when serialized payload > 2048 bytes.
2026-03-11 01:10 UTC - Hotfix deployed to broker-prod-canary disabling experimental tag emission; monitoring showed drop in failure rate.
2026-03-11 20:30 UTC - Confirmed that affected GCP SA subset included longer requestor identifiers from an onboarding automation tool; these pushed payload over threshold.
2026-03-12 09:00 UTC - Drafted compacting mapping and unit tests; preparing PR against agent-auth/broker (see related_github_prs).
workaround: Broker hotfix: disable experimental/verbose session tagging for federated WIF flows (deployed to canary/prod). Operators may also pre-run a tag-compact step in the onboarding script to shorten requestor_id values for affected service accounts.
resolution: Ongoing - hotfix reduced failure rate but full fix requires broker tag compacting + env-provisioner hardening. Target rollout for full fix in the next release window.
